benchmark: t4-belief v1 (20 hidden-information puzzles, engine-admitted 20/20 xmage)
comparison: haiku 7 seeds: arm a (single answer) vs arm c (search, 3-5 candidates, linear-value argmax), responses BELIEVED (believe.py), not enumerated
model: claude-haiku-4-5 (in-session subagents; linear value, no LLM scorer)
grading: xmage strict-choose; a line wins only against every believed opponent response
repair_protocol: bounded repair on validation/format failures only (bad phase, nonexistent permanent name, mis-expressed player target); executed strategic losses never repaired; pre-repair results preserved per run
headline: search beats single-answer on ALL 7 seeds post-repair: 139/140 (99.3%) vs 124/140 (88.6%), exact paired sign-flip p=0.0078 (minimum attainable at n=7); pre-repair 135/140 vs 121/140, p=0.031. The T4 seed-1 exploratory claim replicates: the scaffold, not the model, closes the hidden-information gap.
